generated_policy: APPROVED_PUBLIC only; card-specific relationship plus approved identity table experience; no profile-only fallback

records.rationale: Giada gives White's coordinated creature growth a direct example: she helps cast Angels, and each later Angel enters with counters for the Angels already assembled.
records.modal_explanation: Giada asks you to build the flock in order. Every Angel already in play makes the next arrival larger, while her mana ability helps keep that sequence moving.

records.rationale: Adeline turns each attack into a broader formation, creating a tapped-and-attacking Human for every opponent.
records.modal_explanation: Her power counts your whole creature force, then the attack itself adds another Human at each opposing player or planeswalker. The pressure is organized across the table rather than concentrated in one body.

records.rationale: Myrel protects your turn from many opposing responses, then has each Soldier attack build a larger Soldier formation.
records.modal_explanation: On your turn, opponents cannot cast spells or use artifact, creature, or enchantment abilities. When Myrel attacks, the number of new Soldiers equals the Soldiers you already control.

records.rationale: Talrand turns Blue's instant-and-sorcery plan into a visible board by creating a flying Drake whenever you cast one of those spells.
records.modal_explanation: Holding an instant for the right moment no longer means giving up board development: after the spell resolves, Talrand leaves a flying Drake behind. Blue's patience becomes a growing air force.

records.rationale: Teferi lets your creature cards arrive at instant speed while forcing opponents to act only at sorcery speed.
records.modal_explanation: Flash changes when you can deploy creatures, and the last ability narrows when opponents can cast spells. The card makes control of the turn's timing concrete.

records.rationale: Baral makes your instants and sorceries cheaper, then can turn a successful counter into a fresh card and a deliberate discard.
records.modal_explanation: The reduction applies to your instant and sorcery spells. When a spell or ability you control counters a spell, you may draw one card and then discard one card.

records.rationale: K'rrik makes Black's resource-conversion pattern literal by letting life pay for black mana symbols and rewarding additional black spells with +1/+1 counters.
records.modal_explanation: Each {B} in a cost becomes a choice between mana and two life. K'rrik asks how far you can spend your life total now and whether lifelink will earn enough of it back.

records.rationale: Vilis turns life loss into cards, and can spend two life to shrink a target creature.
records.modal_explanation: The activated ability costs one black mana and two life. Separately, whenever you lose life—including from damage—you draw that many cards.

records.rationale: Gonti looks into an opponent's next four cards, takes one face down, and lets you cast it with mana of any type.
records.modal_explanation: Only one card is exiled; the remaining three go to the bottom in a random order. You may cast the exiled card for as long as it stays exiled.

records.rationale: Torbran adds 2 damage whenever a red source you control would damage an opponent or one of their permanents.
records.modal_explanation: Torbran changes the arithmetic before damage is dealt. Your small red sources become meaningful threats when they damage opponents or permanents those opponents control, rewarding a turn where several modest hits arrive together instead of waiting for one oversized play.

records.rationale: Every other creature you bring in hits each opponent for 2, and Purphoros can turn the whole team more aggressive for a turn.
records.modal_explanation: The damage trigger is for another creature you control entering and reaches each opponent. The activated ability costs {2}{R} and gives your creatures +1/+0 until end of turn.

records.rationale: Neheb converts the life your opponents have lost this turn into red mana after combat, so pressure can fuel the next burst of action.
records.modal_explanation: The mana amount counts all life your opponents lost that turn, and the trigger occurs at the beginning of each of your postcombat main phases. Afflict 3 is separate: a player whose creature blocks Neheb loses 3 life.

records.rationale: Azusa gives Green's land-based growth a direct Commander example by allowing two additional land plays on each of your turns.
records.modal_explanation: Azusa asks you to have lands ready in hand and rewards doing the natural thing more often. Two extra land plays accelerate every later creature and mana commitment without changing what the deck is built from.

records.rationale: Selvala rewards a new creature that is bigger than every other creature, then turns your greatest power into mana.
records.modal_explanation: The entering creature's controller may draw only if its power is greater than each other creature's power. Selvala's mana ability uses the greatest power among creatures you control and can make that much mana in any color combination.

records.rationale: Rishkar grows up to two creatures, then lets every creature you have with a counter help produce green mana.
records.modal_explanation: The entry trigger targets up to two creatures. The mana ability applies to each creature you control with any counter on it, including creatures that received a counter from Rishkar.

records.rationale: Isperia represents Azorius leadership, and her card rewards you with additional information when opponents attack you or your planeswalkers.
records.modal_explanation: Isperia turns an attack against you or your planeswalker into a possible card. Opponents can still act, but aggression now supplies the Azorius player with more information and more options.

records.rationale: Grand Arbiter makes your white and blue spells cost less while making every opponent's spell cost more.
records.modal_explanation: The advantage is procedural rather than explosive: your own sequence becomes easier to execute while each opposing action asks for one more mana. The table has to plan around a rule you established simply by keeping him in play.

records.rationale: Lavinia sets a public limit on oversized noncreature spells and counters a spell cast without mana.
records.modal_explanation: The table can see which actions cross the line: a player cannot evade the cost system or cast beyond their land development.

records.rationale: When an opponent's creature card reaches their graveyard, Lazav can copy it while keeping his name, legendary status, hexproof, and the ability to copy again.
records.modal_explanation: You do not choose Lazav's next identity from your own deck; you wait for an opponent to reveal a useful creature, then turn that loss into your disguise. The table's information becomes Dimir material.

records.rationale: Etrata cannot be blocked, exiles a target creature the struck player controls with a hit counter, then her owner shuffles her into their library.
records.modal_explanation: The attack is covert and selective. Each hit removes one chosen piece and leaves a record toward Etrata's alternate loss condition before she disappears.

records.rationale: The Scarab God turns a target creature card in a graveyard into a 4/4 Zombie token copy.
records.modal_explanation: It selects material from a graveyard and reconstitutes it into an altered working body while its upkeep turns your Zombies into pressure and selection.

records.rationale: Rakdos is the native demon-headliner choice: opponents must lose life before the show begins, then life-loss discounts enormous creatures.
records.modal_explanation: Rakdos cannot enter until an opponent has lost life, so the turn begins with a performance that draws blood. The more life the table loses, the more dramatically he discounts the creatures that follow.

records.rationale: This is a pure flavor-forward Rakdos performance: the demon arrives, the stage erupts, and survival becomes a coin-flip spectacle.
records.modal_explanation: His entrance makes every non-Demon, non-Devil, and non-Imp face its own coin flip. You invite the spectacle knowing your creatures may fall with everyone else's, which is precisely where the risk becomes part of the show.

records.rationale: Prosper exiles the top card of your library for a limited play window and makes a Treasure whenever you play a card from exile.
records.modal_explanation: A temporary opportunity becomes tangible mana if you seize it, keeping the turn moving through risk and reward.

records.rationale: Borborygmos turns combat damage into lands in hand, then lets you discard those lands to deal 3 damage to any target.
records.modal_explanation: Connecting once stocks the next barrage: lands revealed from the top three become ammunition rather than future land drops. Gruul force continues after combat because the landscape itself gets thrown at the next target.

records.rationale: She forces you to abandon 'civilized' noncreature spells in exchange for massive mana for monsters.
records.modal_explanation: Nikya adds one mana of a type the land produced whenever you tap it for mana, but only while you accept her ban on noncreature spells. Building around her means choosing creatures to perform jobs that another deck would give to instants, sorceries, or artifacts.

records.rationale: Ruric Thar must attack when able and deals 6 damage to any player who casts a noncreature spell.
records.modal_explanation: Ruric Thar leaves little room to wait behind utility spells: he charges every combat, and each noncreature spell carries a six-damage price. His Ghor assault turns Gruul's hostility toward over-civilized solutions into a table rule.

records.rationale: Whenever another creature you control enters, you gain life equal to its toughness; Trostani can also populate a creature token you control.
records.modal_explanation: The first token establishes what the community can become; populate lets Trostani repeat that body instead of starting over. When another creature you control enters, you gain life equal to its toughness.

records.rationale: Whenever Emmara becomes tapped, she creates a 1/1 lifelink Soldier token.
records.modal_explanation: Participation in work or combat creates another sustaining member of the group.

records.rationale: Each enchantment you cast gains you 1 life and draws a card.
records.modal_explanation: The enchantment work develops both resilience and understanding, one committed piece at a time.

records.rationale: Teysa Karlov makes your permanents' death triggers happen twice, while giving your creature tokens vigilance and lifelink.
records.modal_explanation: A creature dying is no longer a single transaction: every eligible trigger pays twice. Meanwhile, token creatures can attack without giving up defense and can return life, so the workforce remains useful before and after death.

records.rationale: This version of Teysa strongly expresses Orzhov transaction logic: sacrifice, death, replacement bodies, and exile removal all feed the same contract engine.
records.modal_explanation: A black creature's death leaves a white Spirit behind, and three white creatures can then be sacrificed to exile a threat. Teysa keeps moving bodies between roles until enough small obligations become removal.

records.rationale: Each lifegain event puts two +1/+1 counters on Karlov, and removing six of those counters exiles a creature.
records.modal_explanation: Many small lifegain events can build Karlov faster than one large gain. Once he has six counters to spend, the accumulated payments become a sentence against the creature you choose.

records.rationale: Niv-Mizzet draws whenever any player casts an instant or sorcery, then turns every card you draw into 1 damage to a target.
records.modal_explanation: A spell on either side of the table feeds the experiment. Each new card becomes a precise point of damage, so a long exchange of instants and sorceries lets Niv-Mizzet keep observing and answering at the same time.

records.rationale: Melek preserves the lab-experiment feel without defaulting to the dragon. Revealing the top card and copying spells feels like an unstable experiment becoming repeatable technique.
records.modal_explanation: Everyone sees the top card, but only you can cast a revealed instant or sorcery from your library and copy that spell. Melek makes the experiment public, then rewards you for arranging the library so the next result is one worth copying.

records.rationale: Mizzix captures the escalating experiment: every correctly sequenced spell makes the next experiment cheaper and more dangerous.
records.modal_explanation: Casting a spell above your current experience earns a counter, and every counter reduces later instant and sorcery costs. Mizzix rewards choosing a sequence that keeps reaching just beyond what the last experiment taught you.

records.rationale: Jarad grows for each creature card in your graveyard and can sacrifice another creature to make each opponent lose life equal to its power.
records.modal_explanation: Jarad grows with every creature card already in your graveyard, then can sacrifice another creature to make each opponent lose life equal to its power. Even Jarad's own return asks for a Swamp and Forest, so recovery keeps consuming living resources.

records.rationale: The Gitrog Monster trades a land to survive, permits an extra land play, and draws a card when one or more land cards reach your graveyard.
records.modal_explanation: Land moves through sacrifice and the graveyard into continued development and knowledge.

records.rationale: When another creature you control dies, Meren gives you experience, then returns a creature card from your graveyard at end step when experience permits.
records.modal_explanation: Loss accumulates into a resource that restores a chosen creature over time.

records.rationale: Zegana measures your strongest other creature, enters with that many +1/+1 counters, then draws cards equal to her resulting power.
records.modal_explanation: Casting Zegana too early leaves both halves small. Waiting until one of your other creatures has grown turns that earlier investment into a much larger Zegana and a deeper refill, so Simic improvement happens in stages rather than all at once.

records.rationale: Whenever a land you control enters, Tatyova gains you 1 life and draws a card.
records.modal_explanation: Development of the environment directly sustains you and opens the next option.

records.rationale: Green creature spells set up a creature card on top of your library, while blue creature spells can draw that creature.
records.modal_explanation: The two creature actions form a deliberate sequence: one prepares a specimen and the other retrieves it.

records.rationale: Aurelia attacks with haste, untaps your creatures, and creates a second combat the first time she attacks each turn.
records.modal_explanation: The first charge prepares the second one. Creatures that attacked stand ready again, letting the Legion correct targets, press a weakened defender, or commit a new formation before the turn ends.

records.rationale: A low-cost commander whose mentor rewards attacking and who prevents noncombat damage to your other creatures.
records.modal_explanation: Tajic wants to join the attack: mentor strengthens a smaller attacker, while his prevention shield keeps the rest of your creatures safe from noncombat damage. Advancing the team and protecting it happen in the same formation.

records.rationale: Feather returns an instant or sorcery that targeted one of your creatures to your hand at the next end step instead of letting it stay in the graveyard.
records.modal_explanation: Targeting one creature becomes preparation for another coordinated attack: the spell resolves now, then returns for a later turn. Feather keeps Boros combat tricks in service instead of treating them as one-use bursts.

records.rationale: Directly embodies the 'Eureka' moment of discovery by granting Miracle to all instants and sorceries in hand.
records.modal_explanation: The play pattern is a series of discoveries: on each opponent's upkeep, you can trade away a card for a new first draw, and an instant or sorcery found that way can be cast for its {2} miracle cost.

records.rationale: Represents the college's main protagonist in his 2026 iteration, focusing on the spirit-driven historical research.
records.modal_explanation: Cards leaving your graveyard create Spirits, while Quintorius can discard, draw, and mill to keep that history moving. The graveyard is not a sealed archive; its contents repeatedly return as present action.

records.rationale: When Velomachus attacks, it looks seven cards deep and can cast an instant or sorcery with mana value no greater than its power without paying that spell's mana cost.
records.modal_explanation: Each attack searches seven cards deep for a spell Velomachus can put to work immediately. Its power sets the limit, so making the Dragon larger also expands what the next attack can uncover.

records.rationale: Rootha turns a turn's instant-or-sorcery spellcasting into a visible elemental performance: at the beginning of combat on your turn, she creates a separate flying, hasty Elemental token whose size uses the greatest mana value among those spells cast that turn.
records.modal_explanation: The largest instant or sorcery you cast before combat sets the Elemental's size. Choosing when to spend the showpiece spell also chooses how large, fast, and visible Rootha's performance will be.

records.rationale: Zaffai turns increasingly large instant and sorcery performances into foresight, then an Elemental, then a dramatic random blast.
records.modal_explanation: Spellcraft is staged as spectacle with rising scale: each cast is shaped first through selection, and larger works leave a visible elemental or explosive mark.

records.rationale: Casting an instant or sorcery lets Muddle become a copy of a target nonlegendary creature you control with myriad until end of turn.
records.modal_explanation: Every spell can recast the performer into a different form and turn that form into a multi-opponent display.

records.rationale: Zimone makes mathematical scaling visible: +1/+1 counters reduce the cost of your first X spell each turn, and casting that spell puts two +1/+1 counters on her.
records.modal_explanation: Each turn's first X spell uses Zimone's existing counters to reduce its cost, then adds two counters for a future turn. Zimone turns one solved equation into better terms for solving the next.

records.rationale: Adrix and Nev apply a simple doubling rule whenever your effects would create tokens.
records.modal_explanation: The card makes a mathematical transformation visible on the battlefield: each created set becomes an expanded second set under the same rule.

records.rationale: Primo enters with twice X +1/+1 counters, and base-power-0 creatures that deal combat damage create Fractals with counters equal to that damage.
records.modal_explanation: Starting values and combat results become explicit numerical growth on a new Fractal.

records.rationale: Breena makes social influence change combat: an eligible attack against one of your opponents can draw the attacking player a card while you put two +1/+1 counters on a creature you control.
records.modal_explanation: Breena changes whom the table is willing to attack. Swinging at a player with the highest life can pay the attacker a card, while you decide which creature receives the counters and turns that public argument into your advantage.

records.rationale: Shadrix assigns two different combat-time benefits or costs to two different players, making the table's power relationships a deliberate choice.
records.modal_explanation: The choices do not land randomly or all in one place. Shadrix directs resources, pressure, and growth among different players, then lets those choices shape the coming combat.

records.rationale: Your enchantments entering can tap and goad a target creature, while Aura-enchanted attackers draw you a card.
records.modal_explanation: Placed influence redirects a creature's behavior and turns that directed action into advantage.

records.rationale: Dina makes Witherbloom's practical life-and-death exchange visible: once each turn, sacrificing a creature draws you a card; her separate activated ability sacrifices another creature to gain you life and put that creature's power in +1/+1 counters on a target creature you control.
records.modal_explanation: Dina's sacrifice ability asks which creature's power should become life and counters, while her separate draw trigger rewards the first sacrifice each turn. One body can nourish several parts of the board, but timing decides when every benefit is available.

records.rationale: Willowdusk converts whichever was greater this turn—your life gained or life lost—into +1/+1 counters on another creature.
records.modal_explanation: Both healing and harm become measurable living force. The card then puts that stored change into another body as deliberate growth.

records.rationale: Each other creature you control dying grows Gorma and makes later nontoken creatures enter with extra counters for deaths that turn.
records.modal_explanation: Death directly nourishes the remaining body and the next bodies that arrive.

records.rationale: Rafiq is the clearest Bant champion expression: one worthy attacker receives the force and recognition of the whole.
records.modal_explanation: Rafiq asks the rest of your board to stay back while one creature attacks alone. Exalted support and double strike concentrate the whole formation's strength in a single chosen champion.

records.rationale: Casting a creature draws a card and may put a land from your hand onto the battlefield; Chulane can return a creature you control to its owner's hand.
records.modal_explanation: Creature development repeatedly becomes knowledge, land development, and a reusable piece.

records.rationale: Derevi entering or one of your creatures dealing combat damage lets you tap or untap a target permanent.
records.modal_explanation: Organized creature action continually adjusts the table's working pieces.

records.rationale: Y'shtola links planned noncreature spells and a known life-loss threshold to repeatable card access and pressure.
records.modal_explanation: A noncreature spell costing three or more drains every opponent for 2, immediately meeting part of the four-life threshold that can draw a card at the end step. Esper planning becomes a repeatable question of how to cross that known line each turn.

records.rationale: Aminatou surveils 2 each upkeep and gives enchantment cards in your hand miracle at four less mana.
records.modal_explanation: Preparation arranges future information, then a first draw can turn that prepared enchantment into an efficient execution.

records.rationale: Oloro gains you life each upkeep, including from the command zone, and your life gain can become a card for a payment while each opponent loses 1 life.
records.modal_explanation: A steady maintained resource becomes selective information and pressure.

records.rationale: Kess turns a spent instant or sorcery into one more planned option by letting you cast one such card from your graveyard during each of your turns.
records.modal_explanation: Kess gives one spent spell a second and final use on each of your turns. Choosing the right card from the graveyard means yesterday's answer can become today's removal, protection, or finishing move.

records.rationale: Jeleva exiles cards from every player's library when she enters and can cast an instant or sorcery exiled with her for free when she attacks.
records.modal_explanation: An attack converts material taken from every library into an opportunistic spell.

records.rationale: The first instant or sorcery you cast each turn has casualty 2, letting you sacrifice a creature with power 2 or greater to copy it.
records.modal_explanation: A disposable body turns a chosen spell into a second execution with new targets available.

records.rationale: Prossh turns each cast into a larger visible board, then lets those creatures be sacrificed for immediate power.
records.modal_explanation: Paying more commander tax makes Prossh bring more Kobolds, so repeated casts rebuild the food supply. Any one of those bodies can be sacrificed at once to increase his power for the current turn.

records.rationale: Creature spells with mana value 4 or greater gain blitz, so they can be cast for haste, draw on death, and sacrifice at the next end step.
records.modal_explanation: Large creatures become immediate, expendable action whose ending refills the hand.

records.rationale: Lord Windgrace can discard a land for an additional card, then return up to two target land cards from your graveyard to the battlefield.
records.modal_explanation: Land is spent, recovered, and made active again as a practical resource cycle.

records.rationale: Shalai and Hallar turn creature growth into immediate table pressure by dealing damage when +1/+1 counters are put on your creatures.
records.modal_explanation: Every counter event on your creatures can become damage to an opponent. Shalai and Hallar make growing the board and pressuring the table the same act, so abundance never has to remain passive.

records.rationale: Godsire pairs an 8/8 body with an activated ability that creates another 8/8 red, green, and white Beast token.
records.modal_explanation: The card begins at the same enormous scale it can produce again. Tapping it commits a massive existing body to leave behind another massive body.

records.rationale: Marath stores the mana spent to cast it as counters, then can turn those counters into creature growth, damage, or an Elemental token.
records.modal_explanation: Accumulated natural strength is redirected into protection, direct force, or another living body.

records.rationale: Felothar makes an Abzan defensive board matter in combat: creatures assign combat damage using toughness, and defenders can attack.
records.modal_explanation: High toughness stops being merely defensive: Felothar lets those creatures attack and deal combat damage with the same stat that kept them alive. If a creature must be spent, its toughness also sets how many cards you draw before discarding by power.

records.rationale: Hamza makes each creature already strengthened with a +1/+1 counter reduce the cost of building the next creatures.
records.modal_explanation: A developed board carries its endurance forward: prior strengthening turns into room to keep deploying the community through a long game.

records.rationale: At your end step, Betor turns life gained into counters on another creature and life lost into a return of a creature card from your graveyard.
records.modal_explanation: Both sides of the life exchange strengthen the living or reconnect a dead creature to the present.

records.rationale: Eshki rewards increasingly large creature spells with visible growth, then cards and damage as the creatures cross higher power thresholds.
records.modal_explanation: Every creature spell grows Eshki, but power four and power six are the important thresholds. Sequencing larger creatures turns the same instinctive act—casting the next beast—into cards first and table-wide damage later.

records.rationale: Every creature spell makes Animar stronger and lowers the cost of the next creature spell.
records.modal_explanation: The sequence turns embodied action into growing strength and then into faster further action, keeping creature development active under pressure.

records.rationale: When Ureni enters or attacks, it looks eight cards deep and can put a Dragon from among them onto the battlefield.
records.modal_explanation: A large creature's arrival or attack immediately calls another large body into action.

records.rationale: Kotis turns the graveyard into a constrained resource: one creature can be cast from it each turn by exiling three other graveyard cards as an additional cost.
records.modal_explanation: Each creature you cast back costs three other graveyard cards, and the return puts two +1/+1 counters on Kotis. The choice is which dead card is worth saving and which three you are willing to exile to use it.

records.rationale: The Mimeoplasm turns two creature cards from graveyards into one chosen body carrying the other card's power as counters.
records.modal_explanation: Dead material becomes a selected tool rather than passive history: one creature supplies the working form and another contributes its strength.

records.rationale: When Teval attacks, it mills three cards and may return a land from your graveyard; cards leaving your graveyard create Zombie Druids.
records.modal_explanation: Material moves through the graveyard into renewed land and bodies.

records.rationale: Whenever Zurgo attacks, mobilize creates a temporary tapped and attacking Warrior token.
records.modal_explanation: Zurgo's mobilized Warrior is meant to be temporary. When it leaves after attacking, you draw a card, so each charge spends a body now and returns material for the next attack.

records.rationale: Casting another Vampire creates a Vampire token while Edgar is in the command zone or on the battlefield, and attacking grows each Vampire.
records.modal_explanation: The warband expands before and during combat, then carries that growth into the attack.

records.rationale: Attack-triggered abilities of your permanents trigger an additional time when a creature attacking caused them to trigger.
records.modal_explanation: Committing a creature to combat doubles the force of the attack's coordinated consequences.

records.rationale: Shiko and Narset reward deliberate spell sequencing: the second spell each turn can be copied when it targets a permanent or player.
records.modal_explanation: The first spell prepares the flurry; the second earns either a copy when it has a target or a card when it does not. Jeskai timing appears in the decision about which effect should occupy that second-spell position.

records.rationale: Kasla has convoke, and casting another spell with convoke lets you scry 2 then draw a card.
records.modal_explanation: Creatures cooperate to cast a spell, and that practiced cooperation produces selection and knowledge.

records.rationale: Casting a noncreature spell creates a flying Spirit, and sacrificing a Spirit adds red mana.
records.modal_explanation: Spellcraft creates a visible support force that can be converted into the next burst of action.

records.rationale: Breya enters with two Thopter artifact tokens, then can sacrifice two artifacts for damage, creature removal, or life.
records.modal_explanation: Breya arrives with the two artifacts her activation needs, then asks which result matters now: damage, creature removal, or life. The invention is useful because its pieces can be converted into different answers on demand.

records.rationale: When Sharuum enters, it can restore a target artifact card from your graveyard directly to the battlefield, making a constructed tool available for present use again.
records.modal_explanation: The card’s return is specific to an artifact. What was discarded is not regrown; it is deliberately brought back as a working piece of the machine.

records.rationale: At the beginning of your combat, Mishra copies a target noncreature artifact you control into a hasty Construct, then retires that temporary warform at the next end step.
records.modal_explanation: A standing tool is copied into a working combat form for one turn. The effect treats artifact design as something that can be repurposed into immediate function.

records.rationale: Yidris converts successful combat into volatile follow-up routes by giving spells cast from hand cascade for the rest of that turn.
records.modal_explanation: Yidris must connect in combat before the turn changes shape. Once he does, each spell from your hand can uncover a cheaper spell, rewarding you for using the opening immediately and accepting that the exact chain cannot be planned in advance.

records.rationale: Abaddon converts opponents’ life already lost this turn into cascade for qualifying spells cast from your hand, so a successful push can feed an unpredictable burst of further action.
records.modal_explanation: The turn accelerates after opponents lose life. That loss enlarges the range of spells cast from your hand during your turn that can break open into another cast, making momentum and volatility reinforce each other.

records.rationale: Throes of Chaos repeatedly turns a spent land into another cascade, trading stored material for an uncontrolled new route through the deck.
records.modal_explanation: The same spell can return from the graveyard as long as there is land to discard. Each recast asks the deck to improvise another result rather than follow a fixed script.

records.rationale: As Saskia enters, you choose a player; whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, it deals that much damage to the chosen player.
records.modal_explanation: Choosing one player fixes the objective before combat begins. When a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, that damage is also dealt to the chosen player, so successful creature attacks can contribute to the same concentrated campaign.

records.rationale: Tana turns combat damage dealt to a player into an immediate occupying force: every point becomes another Saproling on the battlefield.
records.modal_explanation: Tana rewards committing to the attack. A larger hit does not only reduce a life total; it leaves behind more bodies to take the ground and press the next combat.

records.rationale: Marisi makes combat damage from one of your creatures reshape the next fight: opponents cannot cast spells during combat, and the struck player’s creatures are goaded.
records.modal_explanation: One opening changes the table from a place to prepare into a place that must act. Marisi keeps pressure moving through the next turn cycle instead of allowing a quiet reset.

records.rationale: At your end step, you draw; each player may put a land from hand onto the battlefield, then each opponent who did not do so draws.
records.modal_explanation: At your end step, you draw first, then each player may put a land from hand onto the battlefield; each opponent who does not put one draws. Playing them means opening resources to the table without giving up your own return.

records.rationale: Collective Voyage lets every player help set the scale of a shared land expansion, then lets each player find up to that many basic lands tapped.
records.modal_explanation: The table can contribute to one common total before anyone searches. The effect makes a public resource decision concrete: the group chooses how large the shared development becomes.

records.rationale: When cast, Wedding Ring gives a target opponent a matching engine and makes that opponent's card draw or life gain during their turn echo back to you.
records.modal_explanation: The card creates a paired arrangement rather than a one-way gift. One player’s ordinary progress becomes shared progress for the other, keeping the benefit visible on both sides.

records.rationale: At the beginning of each of your end steps, Atraxa proliferates the counters you choose to advance.
records.modal_explanation: Atraxa does not create the first counter; she rewards you for placing counters where they will matter before your end step. Proliferate then advances every chosen counter-bearing permanent or player together.

records.rationale: Evolution Sage makes each land entering under your control a careful increment across the counters already in place.
records.modal_explanation: Growth happens in steps. A land entering does not replace the existing work; it advances every chosen counter-bearing project by one more measure.

records.rationale: The Ozolith preserves counters when one of your creatures leaves and can deliberately transfer the accumulated work to a target creature at the beginning of your combat.
records.modal_explanation: A setback does not erase development. The counters wait in one place until a new body can carry their full weight into the next attack.

records.rationale: Omarthis shows one way Colorless can support +1/+1 counter growth: it grows when another colorless creature receives counters, then manifests cards equal to its counters when it dies.
records.modal_explanation: Choose X when you cast Omarthis, then let counter events on your other colorless creatures keep adding to it. Its size and its eventual manifest payout grow from the same accumulated counters, so one colorless counter system does both jobs.

records.rationale: Zhulodok shows the Eldrazi-scale side of Colorless: colorless spells cast from hand with mana value seven or greater receive cascade twice.
records.modal_explanation: The work happens before the seven-mana spell: you build enough colorless mana, keep the large spell in hand, and then accept two unpredictable chains when it is cast. Zhulodok makes scale the trigger for abundance.

records.rationale: Liberator lets you cast colorless and artifact spells as though they had flash, and a spell cast with mana greater than its power grows it.
records.modal_explanation: Colorless construction acts at unexpected timing and turns larger investments into more capacity.

records.rationale: Ulalek's five-color identity opens the deck's breadth; when you cast an Eldrazi spell, its trigger can turn {C}{C} into copies of every spell you control and every other activated or triggered ability you control, except mana abilities.
records.modal_explanation: Ulalek's trigger begins when you cast an Eldrazi and, as it resolves, offers the choice to pay two colorless mana. Paying it copies every spell you control and every other activated or triggered ability you control except mana abilities, turning the stack into a coordinated wave of copies.

records.rationale: The Ur-Dragon reduces other Dragon spells from the command zone or battlefield, and attacking with Dragons draws that many cards then may put a permanent from your hand onto the battlefield.
records.modal_explanation: A developed suite of different Dragons becomes a single engine for cards and permanent deployment.

records.rationale: Sliver creature cards in your graveyard have encore, creating a hasty token copy for each opponent when activated.
records.modal_explanation: A creature stored in the graveyard can return as several coordinated attacks across the table.
